newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police seize CDs in neo-Nazi crackdown.
newsitem.headline: German police seize CDs in neo-Nazi crackdown.

text.p: German police raided targets nationwide and seized hundreds of compact discs on Wednesday as part of an operation to crack down on neo-Nazi recordings by skinhead bands.
The Federal Criminal Investigation Office (BKA) in Wiesbaden said police had swooped on 16 distribution operations, seizing CDs, personal computers and order forms.
They also confiscated wartime weapons, a machine gun and neo-Nazi paraphenalia such as swastika flags.
A BKA spokeswoman said it was too early to say exactly how many CDs had been seized but authorities in the southern state of Bavaria said they alone had grabbed 500.
"This operation had the aim of combatting the increasing supply of recordings with extreme right wing or xenophobic content," the investigation office said in a statement.
German authorities have grown increasingly concerned about a rise in the use of rock music and extremist concerts to spread neo-Nazi messages of racial hatred across the country.
The BKA said the producers of the CDs were motivated by both political conviction and a desire to make money.

"On the one hand, the lyrics express blatant racism and extreme right-wing thinking, which has the effect of stimulating violence," it said. "At the same time, big profits can be made from these products."
